name: master bolognese
instructions:
FOUR BOLOGNESE VARIANTS. All share: tomato base + a protein (real meat, faux meat, mushrooms, or lentils) + acid (wine or balsamic) + soffrito-style aromatics + long simmer intent + pasta. Variant A is the canonical bolognese and gets the headline treatment; B, C, D are vegetarian/vegan reinterpretations that follow the bolognese SHAPE rather than trying to be Marcella's dish.

=== VARIANT A — MARCELLA BOLOGNESE (CANONICAL) ===

The load-bearing recipe in this family. Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking. If 'bolognese' means one thing in this cookbook, it's this one.

INGREDIENTS:
- vegetable oil + butter (the fat)
- yellow onions, celery, carrots — finely diced soffrito
- ground beef (or impossible meat as the substitute)
- milk
- nutmeg
- white wine
- canned tomatoes
- black pepper
- pasta (traditionally tagliatelle, not spaghetti)
- parmesan cheese for serving

TECHNIQUE — MARCELLA'S NON-NEGOTIABLES:
1. Cook the beef ONLY until it loses raw color. Do NOT brown it. Browning gives a different (and lesser) ragu.
2. Milk goes in BEFORE wine. The milk coats the meat and protects it from the wine acid; reversing the order changes the texture.
3. Bare-simmer for THREE+ HOURS uncovered. Splash in water if it dries out. The long uncovered simmer is what makes it a bolognese; cutting time turns it into a generic meat sauce.
4. Fat should separate at the end. That's the visual signal you're done.

=== VARIANT B — NISHA VORA'S LENTIL BOLOGNESE (VEGAN, TOMATO-PASTE-FORWARD) ===

From Nisha Vora / Rainbow Plant Life. Follows a traditionally-bolognese technique (tomato paste caramelized in the fond, red wine deglaze, long simmer, balsamic finish). Red lentils + finely chopped walnuts do the meat-analog work; the tomato paste + crushed tomatoes carry the umami. ~55 min total, much faster than the 3-hour bolognese in variant A.

INGREDIENTS (serves 6):
- 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large onion, diced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp dried thyme (or more oregano if you don't have thyme)
- 1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
- freshly ground black pepper
- 1 (5.3-oz / 150g) TUBE of tomato paste (see notes — tube is load-bearing, not canned)
- 1/2 cup (120mL) dry red wine (optional but recommended — malbec / chianti / tempranillo / sangiovese / merlot / cabernet sauvignon / pinot noir / syrah)
- 3 cups (720mL) vegetable broth
- 1 cup (185g) RED lentils, soaked 30-60 min first (see notes)
- 1/4 cup (32g) walnuts, crushed finely (see notes on chopping)
- 1 (14.5-oz / 410g) can crushed tomatoes OR whole peeled tomatoes crushed by hand
- 12-16 oz pasta (long-wide preferred: tagliatelle, pappardelle, fettuccine; ridged tube also works: rigatoni, penne rigate; gnocchi works)
- 1 tbsp high-quality aged balsamic vinegar (or 1-2 tsp brown/coconut/cane sugar as a sub)
- flat-leaf parsley or fresh basil, chopped, for garnish

PROCEDURE:
1. Soak the red lentils in cool water for 30-60 min. Meanwhile, prep everything else (chop onion + garlic, finely chop walnuts).
2. Heat 12-inch deep sauté pan or Dutch oven on medium-high. Add olive oil; when shimmering, add onions + pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until light-brown fond forms on the pan surface (~5 min). Deglaze with a few spoons of water and stir. Continue cooking, adding more water every few minutes and stirring frequently to prevent burning, until onions are softened and golden brown (9-10 min total).
3. Add garlic, thyme, oregano, 1 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper. Stir frequently, cook 60-90 sec.
4. Stir in the ENTIRE TUBE OF TOMATO PASTE. Cook 2-3 min, stirring very frequently, until it caramelizes and turns darker red.
5. OPTIONAL — DEGLAZE WITH RED WINE: pour in wine, scrape up browned bits, cook 1-2 min until alcohol smell burns off and mixture is jammy.
6. Pour in vegetable broth to deglaze. Add drained lentils and crushed walnuts; stir. Bring to a boil, reduce to medium-low for a rapid simmer, cook 20 min stirring occasionally.
7. Add the crushed tomatoes. Simmer another 15-20 min (or 20 min for more developed flavor) until lentils are tender but still al dente. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. If using crushed tomatoes (not whole crushed by hand), may need a little water or lower heat.
8. Meanwhile, cook pasta in generously salted water to just al dente. Reserve a ladle of pasta water. Drain (don't rinse).
9. Taste for seasoning. Finish the bolognese with the balsamic vinegar (or sugar sub) and stir.
10. Add the hot pasta to the bolognese, toss until coated, add pasta water as needed. Garnish with fresh parsley or basil.

=== VARIANT C — ATK MUSHROOM BOLOGNESE (VEGETARIAN, NO LENTILS, DAIRY) ===

From America's Test Kitchen. Mushroom-forward vegetarian bolognese without lentils — the mushrooms carry the whole 'meat' slot, and dairy (heavy cream, per variant A's protective-dairy logic) plus soy sauce plus porcini mushroom powder do the umami.

INGREDIENT LIST (procedure omitted — see ATK source for the full recipe):
- mushrooms
- carrot
- onion
- butter
- canned tomatoes
- porcini mushroom powder
- garlic
- sugar
- tomato paste
- red wine
- vegetable broth
- soy sauce
- heavy cream
- salt and black pepper

=== VARIANT D — MY VEGETARIAN MIX (BORROWED FROM A + B + C) ===

My own vegetarian bolognese that pulls from the other variants. Mushroom + lentil dual protein slot, with a marcella-shaped soffrito + milk base, ATK's umami adds, and Nisha's balsamic finish.

WHAT'S BORROWED FROM WHERE:
- From variant A (Marcella): finely diced onion + carrot + celery soffrito, nutmeg, MILK (before the wine).
- From variant B (Nisha): lentils in a bolognese format, balsamic vinegar finish.
- From variant C (ATK): diced mushrooms as a real structural component, porcini mushroom powder, tomato-paste-plus-canned-tomatoes umami base.
- MY SWAPS: BROWN lentils instead of red (Nisha's default), and MISO PASTE instead of soy sauce (ATK's default) — same fermented-salty umami slot, but miso stays closer to italian/european register than soy sauce does.

INGREDIENT LIST:
- olive oil (or butter, per Marcella)
- onion, carrot, celery — finely diced (Marcella-style soffrito)
- garlic
- mushrooms, diced
- BROWN lentils (not red — see notes)
- canned tomatoes
- tomato paste
- porcini mushroom powder
- MISO paste (in place of ATK's soy sauce)
- balsamic vinegar (finish)
- milk (before the wine, per Marcella's rule)
- PINOT NOIR (dry red wine — I keep forgetting to add this)
- nutmeg
- BLACK PEPPER (also easy to forget)
- salt
- pasta

See notes for failure modes and current want-to-try items.
notes:
THE BOLOGNESE SHAPE — WHAT THESE FOUR HAVE IN COMMON:
1. A tomato base (canned tomatoes + often tomato paste; regular canned only — no fire-roasted; that's fire-roasted-meatballs.json).
2. A protein slot: real meat (A), lentils + walnuts (B), mushrooms (C), mushrooms + lentils (D).
3. An acid: white wine (A), red wine + balsamic (B), red wine (C, D).
4. Soffrito-style FINELY DICED aromatics: yellow onion always in; celery/carrot/garlic vary.
5. Long simmer intent (3+ hours for A; ~55 min for B; ATK's own long timeline for C; roughly Nisha-length for D).
6. Dairy in most of them — milk (A, D) or heavy cream (C). Nisha's B is the outlier; a commenter noted the sauce could use a dairy component.
7. Served over pasta.

DISTINCTION FROM VEGETABLE-RAGU: the vegetable-ragu recipe (eggplant ragu + mushroom lentil ragu) used to live here. It was split off because those aren't bolognese-shaped: no milk-before-wine, no long simmer intent, no dairy component, and the protein slot leans harder on eggplant + shorter-technique mushroom prep. Same italian-pasta family, different shape.

DISTINCTION FROM FIRE-ROASTED-MEATBALLS: also split off. That dish uses fire-roasted tomatoes (load-bearing) and the meatball shape (load-bearing). Neither belongs in bolognese-shape.

DISTINCTION FROM LENTIL-MUSHROOM-STEW: that dish is a stew, not a ragu — broth-forward, served as a soup, explicitly anti-canned-tomato and anti-tomato-paste, uses stock not pasta. It has overlapping headline ingredients with variant D but contradictory rules. Don't merge.

WHY BOLOGNESE GETS THE HEADLINE: variant A is the canonical italian ragu — Marcella Hazan's recipe is the cookbook's reference point. The three non-negotiables (don't brown the beef, milk before wine, three-hour uncovered simmer) define what 'bolognese' means here. Variants B, C, D borrow the bolognese shape but don't try to be bolognese — they're distinct vegetarian/vegan dishes that respect the shape, not vegetarianized copies of Marcella.

FAUX MEAT FOR VARIANT A: impossible meat works as a substitute for ground beef. Don't substitute ground vegan meat for ground beef in bolognese — impossible has the right fat profile, ground vegan meat reads off.

NO FIRE-ROASTED TOMATOES IN THIS FILE: regular canned tomatoes only. Fire-roasted is the signature of fire-roasted-meatballs.json — reading too smoky against the milk-and-nutmeg base (A) or the more classical bolognese registers (B, C, D).

HERB FINISH — SPARINGLY, BY VARIANT: variant A doesn't take fresh herb finishes well (long simmer + milk-and-nutmeg is its own register). Variants B and D can take a chopped parsley or basil garnish (Nisha calls for it in B; my mix in D can go either way). Variant C is per ATK's spec.

TAGLIATELLE OVER SPAGHETTI FOR VARIANT A: Marcella was explicit that bolognese is for tagliatelle, not spaghetti. The wide flat noodle holds the meat sauce; spaghetti slides under it. Variants B, C, D are more forgiving — long-cut still preferred but ridged tubes (rigatoni, penne rigate) work fine.

GRUYERE OVER PARMESAN FOR GRATING ON TOP — MY PREFERENCE: I prefer grated gruyere over grated parmesan as the finishing cheese. The funkiness agrees with the sauce.

=== VARIANT B NOTES — NISHA VORA'S LENTIL BOLOGNESE ===

SOURCE: Nisha Vora, Rainbow Plant Life. 10-ingredient vegan lentil bolognese. ~55 min total (much faster than variant A's 3+ hours).

TOMATO PASTE FROM A TUBE, NOT A CAN — LOAD-BEARING: Nisha is explicit and I trust her on this — canned tomato paste leaves a tinny metallic flavor here that ruins the sauce. Tube tomato paste (Amore, Cento, Mutti, San Merican; Whole Foods 365 or Trader Joe's for budget) is cooked at lower temp and preserved with salt (canned is preserved with citric acid) — brighter, truer tomato flavor. This isn't a nitpick; use a tube.

RED LENTILS SOAKED FIRST — 30 MIN MINIMUM: soaking softens the lentils and cuts the cook time significantly. Skip and they'll take 45-60 min to soften in the sauce instead of ~20 min. Red split lentils (masoor dal from indian groceries) cook even faster. Brown or green lentils work as a sub but need an extra 5-10 min and give the sauce more bite (less melt-into-sauce).

WALNUTS FINELY CHOPPED — MELT INTO THE SAUCE: crush walnuts in a food processor or spice grinder, or knife-chop very finely. Coarser walnut pieces leave hard bits in the finished sauce (not terrible but not ideal). Fine walnuts add meaty body and blend into the sauce texture.

TOAST THE WALNUTS FIRST (BETH'S TIP, ADOPTED HERE): Nisha suggests toasting walnuts in oven or dry skillet to enhance flavor. Same principle as the lentil-wellington walnut-toasting note — toasted walnut is where the meat-analog umami actually lives.

NUT-FREE SUB: Nisha's options — sauté finely diced mushrooms after the onions, OR add 1/2-1 tsp porcini mushroom powder with the broth. Latter is the cleaner sub since it stays in Nisha's recipe timeline.

BALSAMIC FINISH — QUALITY MATTERS OR SKIP: 1 tbsp high-quality aged balsamic. Nisha is explicit that a cheap balsamic just adds watery sourness and doesn't help. Better to omit than to use cheap balsamic. Sugar sub (1-2 tsp brown/coconut/cane) works if the sauce is too sour without.

RED WINE OPTIONAL — REAL DIFFERENCE THOUGH: 1/2 cup dry red deglaze after the tomato paste caramelizes. Recipe works fine without it, but the wine adds noticeable richness and complements the tomato paste. Any dry red works (see ingredient list for the range).

WANT-TO-TRY (FROM COMMENTS SECTION): reader Julie added grated carrot and fresh tomatoes, said it worked well. Grated carrot in particular is a legitimate soffrito-adjacent addition worth trying — Nisha's original skips the classic mirepoix (celery + carrot), and carrot would push this closer to a traditional soffrito base.

CRITIQUE FROM A COMMENTER: one reviewer (JKL) said the sauce reads too acidic without dairy, felt it needed a milk / dairy component to balance the wine acid. Worth noting if you find the sauce sharp — could try Nisha's balsamic-out / sugar-in path, or (departing from her recipe) add a splash of unsweetened plant milk near the end for a bolognese-adjacent milk protective step.

=== VARIANT C NOTES — ATK MUSHROOM BOLOGNESE ===

SOURCE: America's Test Kitchen. Vegetarian bolognese where mushrooms alone carry the meat slot — no lentils, no walnuts, no ground meat / faux meat. Full recipe not captured here; ingredient list only. Reach for ATK's version for the actual procedure.

WHY THIS BELONGS AS A DISTINCT VARIANT: variant C is the vegetarian version that most closely follows the classical bolognese SHAPE (long simmer + tomato paste + wine + dairy protective step + finely-chopped soffrito), just with mushrooms in the meat slot. This one is 'vegetarianized traditional bolognese' more directly than B or D.

SOY SAUCE + PORCINI POWDER + SUGAR AS UMAMI STACK: ATK's specific move for the umami slot. Soy sauce brings deep salty-fermented umami; porcini powder brings woodsy mushroom concentrated depth; sugar balances the tomato-and-wine acid (same slot Nisha's balsamic occupies in variant B). This is a genuine three-part umami stack rather than the miso+nutritional-yeast pairing common in other vegan recipes.

HEAVY CREAM (NOT MILK) — DAIRY PROTECTIVE STEP: variant A uses milk BEFORE the wine as a protective coat for the raw beef. Variant C uses heavy cream in the finished sauce (later, after the mushroom cook and wine reduction) — different structural moment, different dairy form. The cream is doing an enrichment + acid-buffering role rather than the coat-the-raw-meat role milk plays in variant A. Both are dairy in a bolognese; different jobs.

=== VARIANT D NOTES — MY VEGETARIAN MIX ===

STRUCTURAL LOGIC — MARCELLA SHAPE, VEGETARIAN INGREDIENTS: variant D takes variant A's marcella bolognese SHAPE (finely diced soffrito, milk-before-wine protective step, nutmeg, long-simmer intent) and swaps in a vegetarian protein slot (mushrooms + lentils), Nisha's balsamic finish, and ATK's umami stack (porcini + tomato paste) — with miso replacing soy sauce. Closest structural parallel to variant C (ATK), but with lentils added to the mushroom base.

BROWN LENTILS (NOT RED — DEPARTURE FROM NISHA): variant B uses red lentils specifically because they melt into the sauce. I use BROWN lentils instead — hold more shape, give more bite in the finished sauce, and read more like the ground-meat-shape variant A has. Brown lentils take 5-10 min longer to cook than red, per Nisha's own substitution note in variant B's discussion.

MISO INSTEAD OF SOY SAUCE (DEPARTURE FROM ATK): same fermented-salty-umami slot, but miso reads closer to italian/european register than soy sauce does. Soy sauce works in ATK's version but stays specifically asian-adjacent; miso is more neutral. This is consistent with the miso-in-occidental-cooking principle (see feedback memory): miso lands in western dishes when the vegetable base is diverse enough to absorb it — variant D's onion + carrot + celery + mushroom base qualifies.

MILK-BEFORE-WINE (MARCELLA'S PROTECTIVE-DAIRY STEP) — CARRIED OVER: milk goes in before the pinot noir, per Marcella's rule. Doesn't need to protect raw meat here (there isn't any), but the milk-and-tomato buffer still works — the fat and lactose soften the wine and tomato acid the same way it does in variant A.

DON'T FORGET: BLACK PEPPER AND PINOT NOIR: I keep forgetting to add both when I make this. Written down here so future me remembers. Pinot noir specifically because it doesn't overpower the mushroom-and-lentil base the way a bigger red would (see variant A's wine note — same principle, red wine here instead of white because the mushroom/lentil base handles red better than beef with milk does).

FAILURE MODE — TOO MUCH TOMATO FLAVOR: the combination of canned tomatoes + tomato paste + Nisha-style long simmer has, in my cooks so far, tipped the sauce too tomato-forward. Loses the mushroom-and-lentil character that's supposed to be the point. Next-attempt fixes to try:
- Cut the canned tomatoes back and let the tomato paste carry more of the tomato flavor (paste is more concentrated per volume).
- Or cut the tomato paste back and let the canned tomatoes carry it.
- Or add more mushroom-and-lentil to shift the ratio.
- Or add more milk / possibly heavy cream (see want-to-try below) to buffer the tomato.

WANT TO TRY — HEAVY CREAM INSTEAD OF (OR IN ADDITION TO) MILK: variant A's milk is a Marcella non-negotiable, but variant C (ATK) uses heavy cream instead. Worth trying heavy cream in variant D — could replace the milk entirely, or work alongside it (milk before wine per Marcella + cream at the finish per ATK). Either might help with the too-much-tomato failure mode above; cream's fat is a stronger tomato buffer than milk's.

WANT TO TRY — WALNUTS INSTEAD OF MUSHROOMS (LENTILS STAY): swap out the mushrooms for walnuts in a future attempt at variant D. Lentils have to stay.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- vegetable-ragu.json: eggplant ragu + mushroom lentil ragu. Split off from this file. Different shape (not bolognese) — no milk-before-wine, no long simmer intent, shorter/simpler technique.
- fire-roasted-meatballs.json: also split off. Uses fire-roasted tomatoes + meatball shape (both load-bearing).
- master-italian-tomato-sauce-and-pesto.json: the protein-free italian pasta-sauce family. This bolognese file is the protein-forward, long-simmered, cutting-board-cut counterpart. Everything on the OTHER side of these axes belongs there:
  - PROTEIN-FREE SAUCES AND PESTI: no meat, no faux meat, no lentils. Nuts and cheese fill the fat-and-protein slot over there; the absence of a real protein slot is the tell.
  - FAST (<45 MIN) OR RAW: Hazan's 3-ingredient simmer is 45 min; the halfway-pesto variant is 30-40 min; the sicilian pesto rosso variant is raw and blended in a food processor. Bolognese's canonical time investment (3+ hour bare simmer for A) doesn't fit there.
  - WHOLE-OR-BLENDED, NOT KNIFE-DICED: bolognese's soffrito (finely diced onion + celery + carrot) stays visible in the finished dish. Over there, Hazan halves the onion and discards it, other variants get blended smooth. No discrete chunks survive.
  - PASTA-FINISHER, NOT MAIN-DISH SAUCE: pesto and tomato sauces there are pasta-finishers — pasta and sauce as equal partners. Bolognese is the main event and pasta is a delivery vehicle.
  The cutting-board vs blender/whole distinction is the biggest one. If you're reaching for a knife to dice a soffrito, you're here; if you're halving an onion to fish out or blending everything smooth, you're over there.
